Section 1
The unlikely Twitter feud began innocuously enough during Jeremy Hunt's routine appearance on The Andrew Marr Show two weeks prior. The Health Secretary confidently declared that the NHS had overseen "the biggest expansion of mental health provision in Europe," a bold claim that would soon attract unwanted scrutiny. Among the viewers was Ralf Little, the beloved comedy actor known for his portrayal of Anthony in The Royle Family, who found himself increasingly incredulous at what he was hearing from his television screen.

Section 2
Little's response was swift and uncompromising. Taking to Twitter, he accused Hunt of "knowingly lying" to the public about mental health statistics and boldly challenged the Health Secretary to sue him if his assessment was incorrect. The tweet quickly gained traction, with many social media users sharing and commenting on the actor's direct confrontation with a senior government minister. What made Little's challenge particularly striking was his willingness to put legal consequences on the line for his accusations.

Section 3
Hunt, already under scrutiny for recently having to retract a parliamentary claim about hiring 30,000 mental health workers—a figure that was 43 times higher than reality—waited a full week before responding. When he finally did, it was with characteristic political bravado, presenting a string of statistics and issuing a "double dare" back to Little to prove his counter-claims. The Health Secretary's response suggested he was taking the comedian's challenge seriously, despite Little's background in entertainment rather than healthcare policy.

Section 4
Little's rebuttal was methodical and comprehensive. The actor crafted a thread of more than 40 tweets systematically dismantling Hunt's claims, drawing extensively on research from Full Fact, an independent UK fact-checking charity. The thread demonstrated surprising depth of knowledge about NHS mental health provision and was shared more than 15,000 times across social media platforms. Little's detailed response transformed what could have been dismissed as celebrity activism into a substantive policy debate.

Section 5
Hunt's Monday response revealed the extent to which the exchange had escalated. The Health Secretary posted 26 tweets of his own, though technical difficulties with the chronological ordering made his argument difficult to follow. He questioned Little's credibility while defending his position, citing 8,000 mental health nurses in training and a 25% increase in nursing training places. Notably, Hunt also referenced a New York Times article from July that had been corrected three times following challenges from former shadow minister for mental health Luciana Berger, inadvertently highlighting the ongoing disputes surrounding NHS mental health statistics.
